full_text_en:
Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan — drug trafficking case

Defendant: Wen Yuanhe, also known as Yong Zhandalagong, male, 61 years old, Thai nationality, residing at No. 63-3 Xibing Street, Changkang District, Chiang Mai City, Thailand. Arrested on August 27, 1986.

Defendant: Dai Wenxuan, also known as Dai Yongcun, male, 35 years old, native of Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, residing at No. 396 Yuanzhou Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong. Arrested on August 25, 1986.

Defendant: Yu Xikuan, male, 32 years old, native of Taishan County, Guangdong Province, residing at No. 17, Zhongjian Building, Zhonghui Street, Kowloon, Hong Kong. Arrested on August 25, 1986.

The defendants Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan were indicted for drug trafficking by the Kunming Municipal People's Procuratorate to the Kunming Intermediate People's Court. The Kunming Intermediate People's Court reviewed the case in accordance with Article 108 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Upon review, it was determined that: Among the three defendants in this case, Wen Yuanhe is a Thai citizen. Pursuant to Article 3, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China: "This Law shall apply to anyone who commits a crime within the territory of the People's Republic of China, except as otherwise specifically provided by law." "If an act or its result occurs within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the crime shall be deemed to have been committed within the territory of the People's Republic of China." Accordingly, the People's Republic of China has full jurisdiction over this case. Therefore, the Kunming Intermediate People's Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and conducted a public trial of the case.

The facts found by the court: In early 1986, defendants Wen Yuanhe and Dai Wenxuan colluded with local drug traffickers in Bangkok, Thailand, to jointly plot the trafficking of heroin. Wen Yuanhe was responsible for contacting and concluding transactions with foreign drug traffickers and supervising the receipt and transport of drugs; Dai Wenxuan was responsible for receiving and transporting the drugs through Kunming, Guangzhou, and then to Shenzhen for exit from China. On April 18, 1986, Dai Wenxuan and co-defendant Yu Xikuan arrived in Kunming and met with Wen Yuanhe, who had arrived from Thailand. Together, they met with foreign drug traffickers who had infiltrated Kunming and agreed on the time and place for the drug handover in Kunming. At approximately 6:00 p.m. on August 16, 1986, Dai Wenxuan and Yu Xikuan were receiving drugs at a fruit stall outside the Kunming Railway Station when they were apprehended by public security officers. Heroin weighing 22,768 grams was seized. Wen Yuanhe was also arrested that same evening.

The above facts are confirmed by the seized heroin, the forensic technical identification report, and the testimony of the co-defendants. The facts are clear, the evidence is truthful and sufficient, and the findings are established.

The Kunming Intermediate People's Court held in its trial: The defendants Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan jointly committed the criminal act, which constitutes joint intentional crime as defined in Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Wen Yuanhe and Dai Wenxuan were the organizers, planners, and persons responsible for contacting and receiving the drugs in the joint crime. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, they are the principal offenders in this case and shall be given heavier punishments. Yu Xikuan, induced by Dai Wenxuan, participated in receiving and transporting the drugs. Pursuant to Article 24 of the Criminal Law, he is an accessory in this case and shall be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offenders. The joint trafficking of drugs by Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan constitutes the crime of drug trafficking as defined in Article 171 of the Criminal Law. The above defendants trafficked an extremely large quantity of drugs, and the circumstances of the case are particularly serious. In accordance with Item (1) of Article 1 of the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy," they shall be severely punished. Accordingly, on January 6, 1987, the Kunming Intermediate People's Court sentenced Wen Yuanhe and Dai Wenxuan to death for the crime of drug trafficking; and sentenced Yu Xikuan to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, for the crime of drug trafficking. Pursuant to Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, Dai Wenxuan and Yu Xikuan were respectively deprived of political rights for life. The seized 22,768 grams of No. 4 heroin, two bicycles used for transporting drugs, and two travel bags used for carrying drugs were confiscated in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law.

After the judgment was pronounced, Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan all disagreed with the first-instance judgment, and each appealed to the Yunnan High People's Court on the grounds that some of the facts found in the original judgment were incorrect and the punishment was too severe.

The Yunnan High People's Court publicly tried the case on January 23, 1987. Upon trial, it was held that Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan jointly trafficked 22,768 grams of heroin, an extremely large quantity, with particularly serious circumstances, and should be severely punished. The grounds of appeal raised by Wen Yuanhe, Dai Wenxuan, and Yu Xikuan could not be established. Accordingly, pursuant to Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law, on January 24, 1987, the court issued a ruling dismissing the appeals and affirming the original judgment.

In accordance with Article 145, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Yunnan High People's Court reported the ruling affirming the death sentences of Wen Yuanhe and Dai Wenxuan to the Supreme People's Court for approval; in accordance with Article 146 of the Criminal Procedure Law, it approved the judgment of the Kunming Intermediate People's Court sentencing Yu Xikuan to death with a two-year suspension of execution and deprivation of political rights for life.

The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the death penalty review procedure under the Criminal Procedure Law, reviewed the case and confirmed: The acts of defendants Wen Yuanhe and Dai Wenxuan in jointly trafficking drugs constitute the crime of drug trafficking, and the quantity of drugs trafficked was extremely large, with particularly serious circumstances, warranting severe punishment. The criminal facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance ruling are clear, the evidence is truthful and sufficient, the conviction is accurate, the sentencing is appropriate, and the trial procedures are lawful. Following discussion by the Judicial Committee on February 7, 1987, the court approved the criminal ruling of the Yunnan High People's Court affirming the original trial's sentences of death for Wen Yuanhe for drug trafficking, and death for Dai Wenxuan with deprivation of political rights for life.
